rules_text:
Rules summary 1v1 deck builder ; ~ 25 min ; 8 y+ ; 2 /5 complexity; Football(soccer) game based on Captain Tsubasa. Round Draw to 4 cards. Defending player drafts card from 4 available or deck. Then attacking player drafts . Attacking player plays card or passes . Cards have 1-2 optional abilities ( draw , play , add tokens , delete , etc), which can combo. You cannot use abilities from cards from previous turns (except re-roll dice and goalkeepers, which activate in shoot/pass phase). During this step, you can Motivate (improve) some cards, and Recruit new cards into the play area. Check bench for their token costs. Repeat this step(3) for defending player. Repeat until 9 cards in area or both players pass. Attacking player shoots or passes . Attacking player can add tokens to increase shot/pass, then defending player can add defence. If goal, increase goals by 1. If pass or corner (from shot), keep possession, otherwise change attacking player. Extra rules When the last card is taken in each half, Injury Time begins. Play continues until attacker loses the ball or scores a goal. After the First Half, the match goes to half-time, hand&decks are re-shuffled. After the Second Half, match ends, unless there is a tie, which starts Extra time . Extra time - 2 halves with 2 rounds each (passing still works). Reshuffle at the start of each half. Card limit is 7 . If tied, ends anyway.

[Rating: 3/10] A 2 player card based game where players take turns playing offense and defence. Players can take multiple turns playing cards until they want to resolve their round. [Rating: 5/10] Tsubasa deserves a better game to capture the nostalgia. Unfortunately, this one overstays its welcome. The standard d6 with traditional 1-6 faces is far too swingy, especially when you can lose after investing heavily in a strategy. The excessive luck factor undermines any meaningful planning and can make all your efforts feel pointless — particularly when it also leads to losing hard-earned tokens.
